skill.name: when-releasing-software-use-github-release-management
skill.description: Guides AI agents through GitHub release planning, semantic versioning, staging validation, deployment strategy selection, release notes, rollback, and post-release monitoring.
skill.summary: Structured GitHub release runbook for AI-assisted versioning, validation, deployment, and rollback.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The static Graphviz and Markdown pattern matches are false positives: they are labels, code fences, inline names, or normal local release examples. One medium semantic risk remains because the runbook recommends executing the mutable npx claude-flow@alpha package during release workflows.

remediation.issue: Mutable alpha package execution during release setup
remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow to an audited version and document integrity checks before users run npx commands in release workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable npx Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells users to run npx claude-flow@alpha during release setup. The alpha tag can change over time and executes package code during a sensitive release workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command is explicit and appears in setup and hook guidance. The risk is mutable supply-chain execution, not proven malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Manual releases are error-prone when versioning, testing, deployment, and rollback steps are spread across teams. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a structured GitHub release workflow with validation checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Coordinates release, testing, review, CI/CD, and documentation roles for GitHub-hosted projects.
Guides semantic version selection from commits and existing version files.
Outlines release branch creation, version updates, artifact builds, and staging validation.
Provides workflows for standard releases, hotfixes, production rollout, rollback, and post-release monitoring.
Includes deployment strategy guidance for rolling, blue-green, and canary releases.
limitations: It is guidance only; referenced scripts and templates are not included in the skill package.
It assumes a GitHub project with existing CI/CD, deployment scripts, and permissions.
It does not verify cloud infrastructure, secrets, or production readiness by itself.
Commands can affect production systems and must be reviewed before execution.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Standard Release
use_cases.description: Plan versioning, staging checks, approvals, deployment, publication, and post-release monitoring in one workflow.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Emergency Hotfix
use_cases.description: Guide hotfix branch creation, targeted validation, expedited approval, production deployment, and backporting.

use_cases.title: Improve Release Documentation
use_cases.description: Create changelog content, release notes, rollback notes, and stakeholder updates before publication.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the next GitHub release for my repository. Include version selection, release branch steps, validation gates, and owner assignments.

prompt_templates.title: Create Release Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use recent changes to draft release notes. Separate features, fixes, breaking changes, known issues, and upgrade steps.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Staging
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staging release candidate. Build a validation checklist covering tests, security review, artifacts, monitoring, and rollback readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Canary Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate a canary deployment plan for this release. Include traffic stages, health metrics, rollback triggers, communication points, and final publishing steps.

output_examples.input: I need to release version 1.4.0 next week.
output_examples.output: A release plan with version recommendation, release branch tasks, staging validation, approval gates, deployment timing, and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: A production release failed health checks after deployment.
output_examples.output: A rollback workflow with failure assessment, previous version restoration, smoke testing, monitoring, and post-mortem follow-up.

output_examples.input: Prepare release notes for a feature and bug-fix release.
output_examples.output: A structured release note draft covering highlights, fixes, breaking changes, upgrade guidance, known issues, and contributors.

best_practices: Review every generated command before running it against shared branches or production.
Pin external tooling versions and document required permissions before release day.
Keep rollback criteria, monitoring checks, and stakeholder approvals explicit.
anti_patterns: Running release commands before staging validation and security review are complete.
Publishing a GitHub release without confirming production health after deployment.
Using mutable tool tags or missing scripts without verifying their source.

faq.question: Does this skill create a GitHub release by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides release workflow guidance and command examples that users must review and execute with proper permissions.

faq.question: Does it include the referenced scripts?
faq.answer: No. The package references scripts and templates, but the scanned skill files do not include those assets.

faq.question: Can it support hotfix releases?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a hotfix workflow with branch creation, targeted testing, approval, deployment, and backporting steps.

faq.question: Can it help with rollback planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes rollback detection, execution, validation, monitoring, and post-mortem follow-up.

faq.question: What tools does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes GitHub, git, CI/CD pipelines, deployment scripts, monitoring, and optional claude-flow coordination tools.

faq.question: Is it safe for production use?
faq.answer: It can support production release planning, but commands must be reviewed, tool versions pinned, and permissions controlled.
